(By Sri Harisha A.S., Aga For R-1 To R-5)
 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 And 227
Of The Constitution Of India Praying To Direct The R-2 To 5
Respondents To Consider The Representations Dated
28.10.2015 And 31.08.2024 By The Petitioner As Per
Annexures-F1 To F3 And Further By Directing Them To Pay
The Compensation To The Petitioner Under The Provisions
Of The Right To Fair Compensation And Rehabilitation Act,
2013 Along With The Other Statutory Benefits.
 This Petition, Coming On For Preliminary Hearing In
'B' Group, This Day, Order Was Made Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice K.S. Hemalekha
 Oral Order

The petitioner has approached this Court seeking a writ of mandamus directing respondent Nos. 2
to 5 to consider his representations dated 28.10.2015 and 31.08.2024 (Annexures-F1 to F3) and
further, to pay compensation under the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Rehabilitation
Act, 2013 along with other statutory benefits.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Aga for the respondents.

Nc: 2025:Khc:50836 Hc-Kar
3.

The case of the petitioner is that he is the owner of a land measuring 1 acre 8 guntas in Sy. No.
236/2 (out of 2 acres 24 guntas including 8 guntas of 'A' Kharab) situated at Bannerghatta Village,
Jigani Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bangalore South Taluk, having purchased the same under the registered sale deed dated 04.03.1978.

It is stated that preliminary notification dated 25.06.1977 was issued Sri.Kalappa vs State Of Karnataka on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77988027/
2 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 notifying the entire extent of Sy. No. 236/2 along with other lands for the purpose of development of Bannerghatta National Park, followed by final notification.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that though an award has been passed in respect of 1 acre 8 guntas, the compensation amount was paid to one Sri Laxam Singh, s/o Late Ramswamy and no award has been passed to the remaining extent belonging to the petitioner.

It is further submitted that the name of petitioner has been mutated in the RTC, and despite repeated NC:
2025:KHC:50836 HC-KAR representations made by the petitioner, the same have not been considered till date.
5.
Learned AGA appearing for the State submits that the representations submitted by the petitioner would be considered in accordance with law within a time bound manner.

6. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the claim of the petitioner, this Court is of the view that the grievance of the petitioner would be adequately addressed if necessary directions are issued to the respondents.

Accordingly, this Court pass the following :
ORDER (i) The Writ Petition is disposed of.

(ii) The respondents are directed to consider the representations of the petitioner dated 28.10.2015 and 31.08.2024 (Annexures-F1 to F3) and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, within a period of eight NC: 2025:KHC:50836 HC-KAR weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this order.
Sd/-
____________________ JUSTICE K.S. HEMALEKHA CKL List No.: 1 Sl No.: 44 Sri.Kalappa vs State Of Karnataka on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77988027/
